summary: Shared base of every UI object and window: vtable, intrusive child ring, draw object, layout handles and a state byte. The batch's field list is a union - Ghidra typed many unrelated UI classes as Ui_Object, so every offset above 0x4C is the first field of some derived class.
evidence: Ui_Object_CtorBase (0x001A66A0) builds the ring at +0x18/+0x1C/+0x20, clears +0x24..+0x44 and sets the byte at +0x48 to 1; Ui_Object_DtorBase (0x001A6768) releases +0x38 through vtable+4, clears +0x30 and unlinks the ring; maybe_Ui_Object_SetDrawPriority (0x001A6068) stores +0x2C and pushes it into +0x38; Ui_Widget_SetNamedPaneText (0x001A619C) guards on +0x30/+0x34; Ui_Object_SetNamedDrawParam (0x001A60B8) reads +0x04 -> +0x10 for the pane-name lookup. The evidence base 'ItemList_Iterator' is a mis-inference (a UI object does not derive from an item-list iterator) and is dropped. structs.json lists 350 vtables for this class, which is why the offsets above 0x4C cannot be named: they are Ui_RowObject / Ui_DiveSubObject / Ui_SubObject / Ui_Widget / Ui_Screen fields that Ghidra typed as Ui_Object.

fields.name: vtable
fields.evidence: Written by every constructor in the batch (49 stores, e.g. Ui_Object_CtorBase 0x001A66A0 stores 0x007593A4, Ui_Object_CtorSimple 0x003700F8 stores 0x007657E0, Ui_Object_CtorSmall 0x002B1E0C stores 0x0075EB84); the batch vtable 0x00758568 has ten slots whose bodies are the Ui_Object_* family (0x001A6068 SetDrawPriority, 0x001A60B8 SetNamedDrawParam, 0x001A619C SetNamedPaneText).

fields.name: maybe_ownerResource
fields.evidence: Ui_Object_SetNamedDrawParam (0x001A60B8) reads *(int*)(self+4) and then its +0x10, and calls vtable+0x2C on that to resolve a pane/material name; Ui_Widget_SetNamedPaneText (0x001A619C) uses the same pair. So +0x04 is the resource owner whose +0x10 is the layout resource set. Only 3 writes and 0 reads in the batch, so the name stays maybe_.

fields.name: unknown_word_08
fields.evidence: Two writes only (param_1[2] = uVar1 / param_1[2] = 0) and three reads with no context; the base constructor 0x001A66A0 does not touch it, so it belongs to a derived class.

fields.name: maybe_layoutRef
fields.evidence: Passed by address to 0x005634E0 (release) and to 0x001DAD58 (layout-ref init) in the same shape as the Ui_LayoutRef members elsewhere; seven reads, three writes. The base constructor does not initialise it.

fields.name: maybe_childRingSentinel
fields.evidence: Ui_Object_BroadcastToChildren (0x001A5F9C) loops `piVar1 = self->f_14; while (*piVar1 != self->f_10)` and calls vtable+0x1C on each node, so +0x10 is the sentinel the child ring terminates on.

summary: List-row sub-object: a Gfx_ObjectDesc-derived render descriptor (vtable, inline name, kind/id) extended with four default colour/vector blocks copied from the globals at 0x007E7000 and 0x007E709C.
evidence: Ui_ListSubObject_BaseCtor (0x0038ACEC) chains Gfx_ObjectDesc_Init (0x00193D84: vtable +0x00, second vtable +0x04, name at +0x08, mode +0x18, flags +0x1C, kind +0x20, id +0x24), installs vtable 0x00766944 and stores the owner at +0x28. The eleven Ui_ListSubObject_Ctor_* variants only add a vtable and copy default blocks, so the base class is Gfx_ObjectDesc (44 bytes) rather than the empty base the analyser recorded.

fields.name: vtable
fields.evidence: Ten constructors store a vtable here (0x00766944 from Ui_ListSubObject_BaseCtor 0x0038ACEC, then 0x00760E34, 0x00766910, 0x0076981C, ...); every one of them chains the base constructor first.

The block is a colour or vector default; the exact meaning is not recoverable, so the name only records that it is a default block.

summary: Per-character text/glyph object: a 0x3B8-byte glyph descriptor (colour, size, layer, font) plus the packed glyph handle and the animation binding used when a message window lays out one character.
evidence: Ui_TextObject_CreateMessageGlyph (0x00312EA4) is the only substantive method: it looks the character record up with 0x0063E998, fills the 0x3B8-byte descriptor, packs the glyph handle into +0x40 and registers the glyph. The second function in the batch (0x00566560) is a Gfx_ModelInstance deleting destructor, so the class is only weakly anchored and most offsets are single reads with no context.

evidence: Ui_SlotSubObject_Dtor (0x00329D64) stores the vtable at +0x00, the owner back-pointer (vtable+0x7C) at +0x4C and 0x0076729C at +0xD8, then releases the two tween objects at +0xE0 and +0xE8 through Ui_LayoutRef_Release and unlinks the list node before Ui_Object_DtorBase. Its twin 0x00329DB8 is the same body without the free, confirming the deleting/non-deleting pair.

fields.name: vtable
fields.evidence: Ui_SlotSubObject_Dtor (0x00329D64) stores its vtable argument here (`*self = vtable`); the twin 0x00329DB8 uses 0x00329E00 instead of 0x00329DB0, the deleting/non-deleting pair.

fields.name: ownerBackPointer
fields.evidence: The destructor stores `vtable + 0x7c` here (`self[0x13] = vtable + 0x7c`), i.e. a pointer into the owner object's vtable block - the standard back-pointer to the owning window.

fields.name: vtable2
fields.evidence: The destructor stores 0x0076729C here (`self[0x36] = iVar2`), a second vtable for the embedded sub-object at +0xD8.

fields.name: layoutRef
fields.evidence: Released with Ui_LayoutRef_Release (0x003E04BC): `iVar1 = Ui_LayoutRef_Release(self + 0x38)` - the first of the two tween/layout references the destructor releases.

summary: Layout binding record: the owning screen, the layout name and the bound-layout handle, used by every pane-setup routine to look a layout up in the screen's resource set.
evidence: Ui_LayoutObject_Bind (0x003E0360) releases the previous layout (0x00537714 + 0x0011FCBC), looks the layout up in the screen's resource set with 0x0053649C by name (arg3 or the name built from self[1] through Ui_AnimClip_ParseSections/0x0065D378), attaches it with Ui_AnimClip_PlayFrom and records the owner screen at self[0]. The five callers are all pane-setup routines (Ui_List_InitPool, maybe_Ui_List_UpdateRowA/B, maybe_Ui_GuideWindow_SetCell).

fields.name: ownerScreen
fields.evidence: Ui_LayoutObject_Bind (0x003E0360) records the screen it attached the layout to (`*self = screen`) and clears it when the layout is released (`*self = 0`); it is also dereferenced as `*self + 4` when the old layout is unbound.

fields.name: layoutName
fields.evidence: Passed to Ui_AnimClip_ParseSections (0x00535D3C) to build the layout name when the caller gives none: `Ui_AnimClip_ParseSections(auStack_28, self[1]); if (layoutName == 0) uVar2 = func_0065D378(auStack_28);`

fields.name: maybe_layoutHandle
fields.evidence: Guards the whole bind (`if (self[5] != 0) { ... }`), so it is the 'layout is bound' handle; the actual layout object lives at self[2]/self[3] (0x00537714 / 0x0011FCBC / Ui_AnimClip_PlayFrom).
